title: Tired of expensive licensing and restrictive charting libraries, I built my own zero-dependency financial chart engine with Canvas
author: findingjo
selftext:
Hey everyone,

If you've ever tried building a trading dashboard or a crypto app, you know the drill:

* **TradingView Charting Library:** Powerful, but the advanced version requires strict approval, business verification, and mandatory branding.
* **Enterprise solutions (like AG Charts / SciChart):** Insanely expensive for solo devs and indie hackers just bootstrapping an MVP.
* **Lightweight options:** Often lack smooth interactions, custom indicator layers, or flexible drawing capabilities.

A while ago, I ran into this exact wall while working on my own trading setup. I didn’t want to pay enterprise licensing just to render candles, nor did I want to bloat my bundle with massive dependencies.

So, I decided to go down the rabbit hole and build **TradeCanvas** from scratch.

# What I set out to solve:

1. **Pure Canvas rendering:** Direct control over pixel projection, rendering loop, and double-buffering without DOM thrashing.
2. **60 FPS smoothness:** Viewport culling so panning across thousands of historical ticks doesn't choke the browser.
3. **Clean separation of layers:** Separated the background grid, main candles, crosshair overlay, and indicator pipelines so rendering one doesn't force a full repaint of everything.
4. **Zero vendor lock-in:** A clean, standalone library designed for developers who just want full control of their charting stack.

It's still in active development, but the core engine, multi-timeframe candle rendering, dynamic price/time scaling, and interactions are working.

# Demo & Links:

* **Live Demo:** [https://bonguynvan.github.io/tradecanvas/](https://bonguynvan.github.io/tradecanvas/)
* [*https://github.com/bonguynvan/tradecanvas*](https://github.com/bonguynvan/tradecanvas)

I’m sharing this early to get candid feedback from this sub. How does the zoom/pan feel on your screen? Are there edge cases or performance dips you notice?

Would love to hear your thoughts, feature requests, or technical critiques!

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: splitting the crosshair onto its own layer is the right call, that repaint is what kills most homemade charts. worth saying TradingView's lightweight-charts is Apache licensed though, the approval wall is only on the full library.

replies.author: findingjo
replies.body:
Fair point on `lightweight-charts` being Apache 2.0! However, working on a trading platform setup, `lightweight-charts` hit a wall pretty fast for our needs. It lacks built-in technical indicators, has very limited support for interactive drawing tools (trendlines, fibs, shapes), and working around their internal abstractions for custom overlay features became more painful than building a tailor-made canvas engine from the ground up.

Appreciate the insight though!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: fair, the drawing tools are the actual wall. indicators you can compute yourself and push in as line series, but fibs and trendlines with drag handles is weeks of work nobody budgets for.
